questions: What has management guided for the next quarter or year (revenue, margins, volumes, capex), and how did earlier guidance compare with what was reported?
What drove the latest reported results (segments, price, volume, mix, costs), and how did they compare with expectations?
Are earnings flattered or depressed by one-offs: investment gains, impairments, non-GAAP or non-IFRS adjustments, working-capital swings?
Which government policies, taxes, subsidies, export controls or regulations changed recently, and how do they affect the company?
What major corporate events happened in the last four months (acquisitions, bond issues, guarantees, buybacks, dividends, management changes, lawsuits)?
What are the capex and investment plans, and how are they funded?
What is changing in competition, market share, pricing and customers?
Why has the share price moved recently, and what are brokers and the press debating?
Which dated events are coming up (results dates, product launches, policy dates, meetings)?

Buy-side: Is the +95.8% 1H FY2027 revenue growth sustainable into FY2028, or is it overly dependent on a handful of hyperscaler customers and their AI capex budgets? What order visibility, backlog or customer-concentration disclosure supports guidance?

Credit: What are the terms, counterparties and funding obligations behind the 2026-08-17 material definitive agreement/direct financial obligation and the 2026-09-03 8-K, and could customer financing, guarantees or purchase commitments pressure liquidity if AI demand slows?

Industry specialist: How is NVIDIA defending data-center share and pricing against custom ASICs and merchant competitors as customers move toward rack-scale AI systems, and what is the assumed China/export-control impact in guidance?

Sceptical accountant: How much of earnings is helped by investment gains, non-GAAP add-backs, working-capital swings or supplier prepayments/purchase commitments, and how clean is revenue recognition around customer financing and long-term supply contracts?
Policy/regulatory: Which export-control, tariff or China-related restrictions are most material to the outlook, and what is management assuming for China revenue, licensing and sovereign-AI demand?

forecast.revenue_drivers: FY2027 is anchored by 1H revenue of $177.8bn and the Q3 guide of $108bn, which excludes China data-center compute (E1); our 91.5% growth assumes Q4 sequential growth on Blackwell 300 and networking rather than a flat guide. FY2028-29 growth relies on Vera Rubin/Blackwell ramps, Meta's Vera Rubin and Spectrum-X deployment (E44), the >$35bn RTX Pro 5500 China order (E42), and >$500bn of third-party AI-infrastructure capital (E33), partly offset by hyperscaler custom ASICs (E43) and H200/China restrictions (E27/E28).
forecast.margin_drivers: FY2027 gross margin starts from 75.0% in 1H (E9) and moves toward the 74.0% Q3 guide (E2/E3); H20 inventory charges are largely behind (E12/E15), but H200 China tariffs are not passable (E28) and OpenAI's Jalapeño custom inference chip could pressure pricing (E45/E46). We hold operating margin at 65.2% in FY2027 (1H 65.9%) as scale offsets higher R&D, then fade to 64.2%/63.2% as Vera Rubin/memory costs (E36) and custom silicon mix in.
forecast.vs_consensus: FY2027 revenue growth of 91.5% is slightly above consensus 90.6%, because we use the $108bn Q3 guide and assume Q4 sequential growth from Blackwell 300/networking with no China data-center compute (E1/E10). FY2028 growth of 66.0% is below consensus 68.2% and FY2029 48.0% is below the model's 51.7% fade: we see custom ASICs (E43), China export/tariff limits (E27/E28) and data-center political/power risk (E51/E52) tempering the >$500bn financing and PORTS-Pike pipeline (E33/E30/E59). Our FY2027 EPS is above consensus mainly because we carry the 1H 65.9% operating margin and 5.1% below-line share, partly offset by a 16.0% tax rate (E20), while buybacks lower the share count (E32).
forecast.key_risk: The most likely wrong assumption is the FY2028 growth step-down to 66.0%: the >$500bn third-party financing (E33) and PORTS-Pike/OpenAI pipeline (E30/E59) could convert faster and push revenue above consensus, while a neo-cloud funding/utilization shock (E64) or post-midterm data-center constraints (E51/E52) could cut it. Early proof would be the Nov. 17 Q3 print/Q4 guide (E55/E57), H200 China approval/tariff news (E27/E28), RTX Pro 5500 order conversion (E42), and whether receivables/DSO (E8) or the $279bn memory commitments (E36) rise faster than revenue.
forecast.remainder: The FY2027E revenue forecast implies revenue of 235,684mn for the second half (+88.3% year on year), against +95.8% reported so far this year.

narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA is a data center scale AI infrastructure company operating through Compute & Networking and Graphics segments. Its products span data center GPUs and networking (InfiniBand, Spectrum-X Ethernet, NVLink), gaming GPUs, professional visualization, and automotive platforms. In FY2026, Data Center products were 89.7% of revenue (USD 193.7bn), Gaming 7.4% (USD 16.0bn), Professional Visualization 1.5% (USD 3.2bn), Automotive 1.1% (USD 2.3bn), and OEM/Other 0.3% (USD 619.0mn).

Customers are concentrated among hyperscalers, which accounted for approximately 50% of Data Center revenue in Q1 FY2027, with the balance from AI Clouds, industrial, enterprise and sovereign customers. Regionally, the United States was 69.3% of FY2026 revenue (USD 149.6bn), Taiwan 19.6% (USD 42.3bn), Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1% (USD 19.7bn), and Other 2.0% (USD 4.3bn). NVIDIA competes with fabless AI-silicon designers including AMD, Broadcom, Marvell, QUALCOMM and Astera Labs, and faces growing in-house silicon efforts at major customers.
narrative.financial_analysis:
In 1H FY2027 (to 26 July 2026) revenue rose 95.8% to USD 177,837mn, gross margin expanded 8.3pp to 75.0%, operating profit grew 134.2% to USD 117,270mn, and net profit rose 161.1% to USD 118,010mn; free cash flow was USD 69,987mn. Q2 FY2027 alone saw revenue of USD 96,221mn (+105.9%) and net profit of USD 59,688mn (+125.9%).

Our forecast sees FY2027E revenue of USD 413,521mn (+91.5%, 0.5% above consensus) and EPS of USD 10.12 (+106.5%, 8.7% above consensus), with FY2028E revenue of USD 686,445mn (-0.8% vs consensus) and EPS of USD 16.81 (+5.6%). Over the four years from FY2022 to FY2026 revenue compounded 68.3% and net profit 87.3%; FY2026 ROE was 101.5%, cash conversion 0.86x, and net cash stood at USD 29,103mn at 26 July 2026.
narrative.valuation_overview:
The DCF (50% weight) uses the probability-weighted scenario value of USD 201.67, blending bear USD 83.58 (30%), base USD 232.71 (50%) and bull USD 301.21 (20%); peer P/E (25%) gives USD 305.84 and peer EV/EBITDA (25%) USD 367.24, producing a blended fair value of USD 269.10 (+44.2%). The Monte Carlo median of USD 266.95 with 84% of draws above the price supports the upside, and the P/E history shows today's 38.1x (on last fiscal-year EPS) in the 6th percentile of its five-year range.

Note the model check: our blended value (USD 269.10) is below all 30 broker targets (lowest USD 275.00); the 50%-weighted DCF uses the probability-weighted scenario value of USD 201.67, while the peer P/E and peer EV/EBITDA methods give USD 305.84 and USD 367.24. The reverse DCF implies 40.8% revenue growth versus our base case of 50.9%.
narrative.competitive_analysis: NVIDIA's TTM revenue growth of 105.9%, gross margin of 74.7%, operating margin of 66.2% and ROE of 117.2% compare with peer medians of 44.7%, 56.0%, 21.2% and 28.2%, respectively. Its forward P/E of 11.7x is well below the peer median of 19.2x despite these superior returns. The vulnerability is that hyperscalers such as Microsoft, Google and Amazon are advancing their own AI semiconductors, and OpenAI's Jalapeño inference chip could pressure Nvidia's pricing.
narrative.news_summary: Recent news is dominated by a board-launched independent probe into a foreign espionage case targeting CEO Jensen Huang, which has weighed on the shares. Political risk rose after Democratic midterm victories raised fears of tighter data-center rules, driving a 9.3% one-day fall on 5 November 2026. Offsetting positives include Nvidia's investments in four German startups, a record A$150bn buyback plan, and reports of large China orders for export-compliant RTX Pro 5500 cards. Inventory turnover at a multi-year low of 3.35x and customer in-house silicon efforts are noted concerns.
narrative.report_summary: Management guided Q3 FY2027 revenue to USD 108.0bn ±2%, gross margin of 74.0% ±50bp, and assumes no Data Center compute revenue from China. The 10-Q notes receivables of USD 63.1bn with 60 days sales outstanding, up from 45 days sequentially, due to extended payment terms on large multi-quarter agreements. Key events include the 2 September 2026 agreement to acquire Hugging Face for approximately USD 11.9bn, guarantees of up to USD 105bn for the SB Energy PORTS-Pike campus, and partnerships to mobilize over USD 500bn of third-party AI-infrastructure capital. Risks include export controls, open-source model regulation, customer concentration, and supply-chain constraints.

learner.big_picture: NVIDIA designs chips and systems for AI data centres — 89.7% of FY2026 revenue. Growth is explosive: revenue rose from USD 26,914mn in FY2022 to 215,938mn in FY2026, and 1H FY2027 is +95.8% on a year earlier. Margins are huge (operating margin 60.4% in FY2026) and it holds net cash of USD 29,103mn at 26 July 2026 (total debt USD 33,366mn) and trades at 23.6x trailing earnings versus a 46.4x peer median. The AI rating is Buy; the stock has lagged the S&P 500 over one year.

steps.business: NVIDIA is a semiconductor designer, mostly for AI data centres: Data Center products were 89.7% of FY2026 revenue, with Gaming 7.4%. The United States was 69.3% of revenue and Taiwan 19.6%. That concentration means one end market and a few large customers drive the whole story, so watch hyperscaler spending plans.
steps.growth: Growth is extraordinary but uneven: FY2023 was +0.2%, then +125.9%, +114.2% and +65.5% to FY2026. Read the latest first: 1H FY2027 is +95.8% and Q2 FY2027 alone +105.9%, faster than the half-year, so growth is accelerating. Analysts expect +90.6% for FY2027E (third-party consensus).
steps.profit: Profitability is exceptional: operating margin rose from 37.3% (FY2022) to 60.4% (FY2026), and net margin from 36.2% to 55.6%. ROE of 101.5% reflects high margin and leverage (equity multiplier 1.35x). But cash conversion is 0.86x — profit is not fully turning into cash — and the accruals ratio is +10.9%; the 10-Q explains the receivables build.
steps.safety: The balance sheet is strong but net cash has fallen: at 26 July 2026 cash and liquid investments of USD 62,469mn exceeded total debt of USD 33,366mn, giving net cash of USD 29,103mn (FY2026: USD 54,088mn). Interest cover was 503.4x in FY2026 and the current ratio 3.91x, so short-term obligations are easily met.
steps.cheap: On trailing numbers it looks cheap versus peers: P/E 23.6x vs peer median 46.4x (-49.2%) and EV/EBITDA 22.2x vs 43.9x. But P/B is 19.7x vs 10.8x (+82.8% premium), and its own 5-year P/E history (38.1x vs median 64.1x) is on a different basis, so don't compare the two. Fast growers are usually judged on forward earnings.
steps.worth: The DCF base case is USD 270.21 per share (WACC 12.0%, terminal growth 2.5%), with a sensitivity range of USD 233.50–320.72. The price implies +40.8% annual growth versus +50.9% in the base case, and 84% of Monte Carlo draws sit above the price. The AI rating is Buy, fair value USD 269.10 (+44.2%); the model changed from Sell to Buy since the last report because of a method or input change, not just the price.
steps.others: Brokers are positive: 30 covering, 16 Buy and 14 Outperform, median target USD 322.50 (+72.8% vs the price); these are broker opinions, not facts. The model's blended fair value of USD 269.10 sits below every one of the 30 broker targets (lowest USD 275.00), with a DCF that uses a 12.0% WACC and a revenue path that fades after FY2028; the model check says not to present the fair value as reliable.
steps.wrong: The stock has lagged: 1-year return -0.5% vs S&P 500 +9.8%, with a max drawdown of -24.1% and volatility of 38.4%. The technical picture is bearish. Press reports attribute the recent fall to worries about data-centre spending, debt-financed AI infrastructure and politics after the midterms; the annual report's risk factors cover China export rules and customer concentration.

discussion: Revenue is +95.8% in 1H FY2027 but cash conversion is only 0.86x — what does that gap tell you, and where would you check?
The stock trades at 23.6x trailing earnings versus a 46.4x peer median, yet P/B is a premium — which multiple best fits a fast-growing chip designer?
Brokers' median target is USD 322.50 while the model's fair value is USD 269.10 — what assumptions could explain the gap, and which would you trust?

company.description: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
